From preprocessed runs to whole-brain group maps

Source: vignettes/whole-brain.Rmd
whole-brain.Rmd

This walkthrough estimates the group mean faces minus houses in a study with two fMRI runs per participant and one visit. Both conditions occur in each run. We fit one FSL FEAT model per run, combine the two run contrasts within participant, and fit a whole-brain group model. The completed maps feed the FWE correction and beta extraction walkthroughs. Use your own preprocessed NIfTIs and event timing with the example below.

Pipeline level Unit of analysis Estimate passed forward
L1, facehouse One run Face coefficient minus house coefficient and its estimated variance
L2, run_average One participant and visit Fixed-effects combination of the retained run contrasts
L3, group_mean One map per participant in the group fit Group COPE and z-statistic for the mean of the participant contrasts

For data with several visits, choose the subject/session structure before fitting. See longitudinal analyses. To run the time-series and group models with AFNI or SPM, see choosing a GLM engine.

Prepare the analysis inputs

You need a working R installation with fmri.pipeline, FSL on the execution host, and preprocessed BOLD data. Supply runs in a common volumetric template space and on a common voxel grid for group analysis. Check the template, orientation, field of view, and voxel sizes. Matching dimensions alone cannot establish that two images are aligned. Keep intensity scaling and preprocessing consistent across the sample. If you use BrainGnomes, select a single postprocessing stream and pair each selected BOLD file with the confound table for the same retained volumes. BrainGnomes postprocessing guide

Create these three CSVs under inputs/. The rows are examples of the schema. Supply all participants, runs, and trials. Use absolute paths that are also visible to compute jobs.

trials.csv has one row per trial in this task. Times are in seconds relative to the start of the supplied BOLD run. The first trial can start at zero. Rest between stimuli is captured by the baseline.

id session run_number trial onset duration condition
01 1 1 1 8.0 2.0 face
01 1 1 2 15.5 2.0 house
01 1 2 1 10.0 2.0 house

runs.csv has one row per id, session, and run_number. Each TSV has one row per volume of the corresponding input NIfTI and columns csf and white_matter in this example.

id session run_number run_nifti confound_input_file
01 1 1 /study/derivatives/sub-01_run-1_bold.nii.gz /study/derivatives/sub-01_run-1_confounds.tsv
01 1 2 /study/derivatives/sub-01_run-2_bold.nii.gz /study/derivatives/sub-01_run-2_confounds.tsv

subjects.csv has one row per participant here. Include group-level predictors in this table when the L3 formula calls for them.

id session
01 1
02 1

Read identifiers as characters to retain leading zeros. Check for unmatched keys so that a mistyped identifier or run number cannot silently change the sample. Verify that both conditions are represented in every modeled run.

library(fmri.pipeline)
library(dplyr)

visit_cols <- readr::cols(
  id = readr::col_character(), session = readr::col_integer()
)
run_cols <- readr::cols(
  id = readr::col_character(), session = readr::col_integer(),
  run_number = readr::col_integer()
)
trial_df <- readr::read_csv("inputs/trials.csv", col_types = run_cols)
run_df <- readr::read_csv("inputs/runs.csv", col_types = run_cols)
subject_df <- readr::read_csv("inputs/subjects.csv", col_types = visit_cols)

visit_key <- c("id", "session")
run_key <- c(visit_key, "run_number")

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(run_df[run_key]), !anyNA(trial_df[run_key]),
  !anyNA(subject_df[visit_key]),
  !anyDuplicated(run_df[run_key]), !anyDuplicated(subject_df[visit_key]),
  nrow(anti_join(trial_df, run_df, by = run_key)) == 0L,
  nrow(anti_join(run_df, trial_df, by = run_key)) == 0L,
  nrow(anti_join(run_df, subject_df, by = visit_key)) == 0L,
  all(file.exists(run_df$run_nifti)),
  all(file.exists(run_df$confound_input_file)),
  all(is.finite(trial_df$onset) & trial_df$onset >= 0),
  all(is.finite(trial_df$duration) & trial_df$duration >= 0),
  all(trial_df$condition %in% c("face", "house"))
)

trial_counts <- trial_df |>
  count(id, session, run_number, condition) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

stopifnot(
  all(c("face", "house") %in% names(trial_counts)),
  all(trial_counts$face > 0 & trial_counts$house > 0)
)

Compare the last event offset to run length (stored volumes × TR) and check that confound rows match the NIfTI volume count. If preprocessing already removed leading volumes, align event times and nuisance rows to those files and leave drop_volumes = 0L. When asking the pipeline to remove volumes, supply inputs and timing aligned to the image before the pipeline drops volumes. See the input reference and confounds guide for more input options.

Define the contrasts at each level

Save the following as facehouse.yaml. The named weights explicitly define the L1 comparison. A positive COPE indicates a larger estimated face response. The L2 and L3 intercept models each produce a single contrast, EV_Intercept. Its input differs by level. L2 averages the two run effects and L3 estimates the sample mean of the resulting participant effects.

onsets: [onset]
durations: [duration]
events:
  stim:
    onset: onset
    duration: duration
signals:
  face:
    event: stim
    trial_subset_expression: "condition == 'face'"
    value_fixed: 1
    normalization: none
  house:
    event: stim
    trial_subset_expression: "condition == 'house'"
    value_fixed: 1
    normalization: none
l1_models:
  facehouse:
    signals: [face, house]
    contrasts:
      diagonal: false
      custom:
        faces_minus_houses: {face: 1, house: -1}
l2_models:
  run_average:
    level: 2
    model_formula: "~ 1"
    l2_scope: id_session
    contrasts:
      diagonal: true
l3_models:
  group_mean:
    level: 3
    model_formula: "~ 1"
    l3_input_mode: per_session
    fsl_outlier_deweighting: false
    contrasts:
      diagonal: true

Use the model builder guide to add condition effects, custom contrasts, or covariates. Each added L1 or L2 contrast can produce another group fit. Decide which group contrast answers the primary question before looking at the maps.

Build and inspect the first-level designs

Set output_root to a directory you can write to on your analysis filesystem. For FEAT batch estimation, use scheduler = "slurm" as shown here, or use "torque" on a Torque system. Set the compute environment so jobs can load R, fmri.pipeline, and FSL. The TR here is 2 seconds. Set it to the actual value for your data, or supply run_df$tr when it differs across participants or visits. Use a consistent TR across runs that belong to one participant and visit.

output_root <- "/study/analysis"

gpa <- setup_glm_pipeline(
  analysis_name = "facehouse_group",
  output_directory = output_root,
  scheduler = "slurm",
  glm_software = "fsl",
  trial_data = trial_df,
  run_data = run_df,
  subject_data = subject_df,
  tr = 2,
  n_expected_runs = 2L,
  drop_volumes = 0L,
  confound_settings = list(
    l1_confound_regressors = c("csf", "white_matter")
  ),
  parallel = list(l1_setup_cores = 1L, l2_setup_cores = 1L),
  additional = list(
    feat_l2_args = list(featwatcher_yn = 0L),
    feat_l3_args = list(featwatcher_yn = 0L)
  ),
  l1_models = NULL, l2_models = NULL, l3_models = NULL
)
gpa <- build_l1_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "facehouse.yaml")
gpa <- build_l2_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "facehouse.yaml")
gpa <- build_l3_models(gpa, from_spec_file = "facehouse.yaml")

The FEAT settings above leave report files on disk without opening a browser from a batch job.

For a design review before estimation, finalize the configuration and write the first-level setup files on a host with FSL and the study data. The following steps write analysis files and may prepare run images and nuisance regressors. FEAT estimation starts at submission.

gpa <- finalize_pipeline_configuration(gpa)
gpa <- setup_l1_models(gpa, l1_model_names = "facehouse")

gpa$l1_model_setup$metadata |>
  select(id, session, run_number, run_volumes, l1_confound_file, exclude_run)

l1_setup <- gpa$l1_model_setup$fsl |>
  filter(l1_model == "facehouse")
readLines(l1_setup$feat_fsf[[1L]]) |>
  grep(pattern = "evtitle|conname|con_real", value = TRUE)

collinearity <- extract_l1_collinearity(gpa, l1_model_names = "facehouse")
head(collinearity$high_correlation)
head(collinearity$high_vif)

Check that the expected runs survived, that each condition regressor has variation, and that the face and house weights have the intended signs. Review event alignment and high-pass filtering against the task timing. Inspect any high correlations or VIFs alongside the underlying design. The generated FSF shows what FEAT was asked to fit. After estimation, design.mat, design.con, and the FEAT report let you review the design that was fitted.

Run and reload the analysis 

run_glm_pipeline(
  gpa,
  l1_model_names = "facehouse",
  l2_model_names = "run_average",
  l3_model_names = "group_mean"
)

diagnose_pipeline(gpa)

On a scheduler, submission returns before the fits complete. Inspect the submission in diagnose_pipeline() and wait for the group fit and cleanup steps before using the common cache. For a failed job, follow the diagnosis guide to identify the first failing step and its logs.

Reload the batch you just checked. The example reads the last recorded submission for this analysis directory. If several people or scripts submit to the same project, select the recorded batch for the run you inspected.

history <- jsonlite::read_json(gpa$output_locations$project_config_json)$batch_history
batch_dir <- tail(history, 1L)[[1L]]$batch_directory[[1L]]
cache <- new.env()
load(file.path(batch_dir, "run_pipeline_cache.RData"), envir = cache)
gpa <- cache$gpa

Find the group map and its inputs

Use lookup_feat_outputs() to resolve names to files. The suffix in zstat1.nii.gz is local to the FEAT fit. Keep the session, model, and contrast names together when selecting or recording a map.

feat <- lookup_feat_outputs(
  gpa, level = c(2L, 3L), what = c("cope", "zstat"),
  source = "setup", refresh_status = TRUE
)

group_map <- feat$l3 |>
  filter(
    session == 1L, l1_model == "facehouse",
    l1_cope_name == "faces_minus_houses",
    l2_model == "run_average", l2_cope_name == "EV_Intercept",
    l3_model == "group_mean", l3_cope_name == "EV_Intercept",
    statistic == "zstat", analysis_status == "complete", image_exists
  )
stopifnot(nrow(group_map) == 1L)
group_map |>
  select(image_file, image_feat_dir, feat_requested_estimator, feat_actual_estimator)

group_mask <- file.path(group_map$image_feat_dir, "mask.nii.gz")
stopifnot(file.exists(group_mask))

analysis_status describes the fit and image_exists describes the individual image. Check both before using a map. Compare requested and actual FEAT estimators to see whether the fit used a fallback. To audit the L3 sample, inspect the input filenames in the group FSF and compare them with the completed L2 COPEs. The FSF records the images in design-row order.

grep("^set feat_files", readLines(group_map$analysis_fsf), value = TRUE)

feat$l2 |>
  filter(
    l1_model == "facehouse", l1_cope_name == "faces_minus_houses",
    l2_model == "run_average", l2_cope_name == "EV_Intercept", statistic == "cope"
  ) |>
  select(id, session, analysis_status, is_passthrough, image_exists, image_file)

A participant with only one usable run may appear as an L2 passthrough. The inventory points to the underlying L1 COPE and marks the logical L2 row as is_passthrough. Review which participants actually entered L3 before reporting the sample size. Inspect the model mask and the spatial pattern of the group maps in a NIfTI viewer.

Use the group z-statistic and its model mask for FWE correction. Use the participant COPEs to summarize effects in ROIs, and the group COPE when the quantity of interest is the fitted sample effect.
